We get a version of this argument in the reading today from Ruth Benedict, one of the most important American anthropologists of the 20th century.
A better argument for moral relativism is the argument from moral disagreement.

Benedict gives us in this paper an impressive list of moral disagreements between various cultures. Notably, we do not find disagreement of this sort about, for example, whether the sky is blue. So, we might ask: Why is there widespread moral disagreement of the sort we find in the world?
